title: Parity, Sensitivity, and Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2602.05896v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Understanding what neural architectures can and cannot compute is a central challenge in the theory of AI. One of the fundamental problems in this context is the PARITY task, which asks whether the number of 1s in a binary input sequence is even or odd. PARITY is one of the central tasks studied in the theory of computation, yet it remains surprisingly unclear under which conditions transformers can or cannot solve it.   In this paper, we show that the minimal number of layers a transformer needs to compute PARITY is two. In particular, we solve the open problem asking whether a one-layer transformer can compute PARITY. We answer it negatively by showing that average sensitivity of a one-layer transformer grows slower than that of PARITY. translated_abstract: arXiv:2602.05896v3 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：理解神经架构能够计算什么、不能计算什么，是人工智能理论中的核心挑战。在这一背景下，一个基础性问题就是奇偶性（PARITY）任务，即判断二进制输入序列中1的个数是偶数还是奇数。PARITY是计算理论中研究的核心任务之一，然而关于transformer在何种条件下能够或不能够解决该问题，目前仍然出人意料地不明确。在本文中，我们证明了transformer计算PARITY所需的最小层数为两层。特别地，我们解决了一个开放性问题：单层transformer是否能够计算PARITY。我们给出了否定的答案，其证明方法是表明单层transformer的平均敏感度增长速度慢于PARITY任务所需的水平。此外，我们提出了一种计算PARITY的transformer新构造，通过移除若干不切实际的假设，改进了现有的构造。
tldr: 本论文证明transformer计算奇偶性任务至少需要两层，从而否定地解决了“单层transformer能否计算奇偶性”这一开放问题，并提出了一种去除不切实际假设的新构造方法。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that a transformer needs at least two layers to compute PARITY, negatively resolving the open problem of whether a one-layer transformer can solve it, and introduces a new construction that removes several impractical assumptions.
